hints: Focus on what actually makes a molecule hard to react, the energy needed to break its bond to start a reaction.
Check statement 1 first. Remember $	ext{N}_2$ has a $	ext{N} \equiv \text{N}$ triple bond with a very high bond energy of about 944 kJ mol$^{-1}$.
Now test statements 2 and 3 for factual errors by asking if $	ext{O}_2$ and $	ext{Cl}_2$ really have polar bonds or incomplete octets.
walkthrough:
**Think about why nitrogen is so inert**

Nitrogen is unreactive mainly because of kinetics, not because it cannot react. It takes a huge amount of energy to break the bond and form reactive atoms or radicals.

Bond strength order:
$$\text{N} \equiv \text{N} > \text{O}=\text{O} > \text{Cl}-\text{Cl}$$

**Check statement 1**

Statement 1 is true and relevant. The $	ext{N} \equiv \text{N}$ triple bond is very short and very strong, so the activation energy for most reactions is very high.

This alone helps explain the difference in reactivity.

**Check statement 2**

Statement 2 is false. A bond between two identical atoms cannot be polar because there is no electronegativity difference.

$$\text{N}_2, \text{O}_2 \text{ and } \text{Cl}_2 \text{ all have non-polar covalent bonds}$$

**Check statement 3**

Statement 3 is false. In all three molecules each atom achieves a full outer shell by sharing electrons.

$\text{N}_2$ : each N has 8 electrons, $\text{O}_2$ : each O has 8 electrons, $\text{Cl}_2$ : each Cl has 8 electrons.

So only statement 1 explains the difference.

options.A: Incorrect. This would mean all three statements are correct. Statements 2 and 3 are factually wrong, so this combination cannot be right.
options.B: Incorrect. This would include statement 2. The bonds in $\text{O}_2$ and $\text{Cl}_2$ are non-polar, just like in $\text{N}_2$, because they join identical atoms. Polarity does not explain the reactivity difference.
options.C: Incorrect. This would include statements 2 and 3 only. Both are false. All three molecules have non-polar bonds and all atoms have complete octets through sharing.
options.D: Correct. Only statement 1 is true and relevant. The very strong $\text{N} \equiv \text{N}$ triple bond makes $\text{N}_2$ kinetically inert compared with $\text{O}_2$ and $\text{Cl}_2$.
